walkthroughs.body_html:
When two waves meet, their displacements add.

Same phase → constructive (loud, bright).
Opposite phase → destructive (silent, dark).

Sources must be coherent (same f, fixed phase relationship).

Light through 2 slits + screen → bright/dark fringes.

Bright (max): path difference Δd = nλ (n = 0, 1, 2, …).
Dark (min): Δd = (n + ½)λ.

Fringe spacing: s = λD/a
where D = slit-screen distance, a = slit separation.

Confirmed wave nature of light (Young, 1801).

Waves spread when they pass through apertures of size ~λ.

Single slit diffraction: minima at sinθ = nλ/b (b = slit width).

Diffraction grating with N slits: maxima at nλ = d sinθ (d = slit spacing).

Sharp, well-spaced — used in spectroscopy.

When does an electron behave as a wave?
options: Charge was created by friction and pulled the balloon to the wall.
Electrons are always waves and only look like particles at low energy.
In experiments that probe wave properties (e.g. diffraction through a crystal); in particle-like experiments it behaves as a particle.
Electrons are sometimes waves and sometimes particles depending on the temperature of the apparatus.

mcqs.q: When you rub a balloon and stick it to the wall, what has been transferred?
options: Electrons have been transferred between the balloon and the cloth (not the wall).
Protons jumped from the balloon to the wall, causing static cling.
Only when the force is small enough to be ignored.
Charge was created by friction and pulled the balloon to the wall.
